item.title: Fiona the hippo's tragic death prompts Cincinnati Zoo to install new safeguards at Hippo Cove
item.description: New safety protections have been introduced at Hippo Cove as the Cincinnati Zoo reopens following Fiona's death, with guests urged to secure belongings.
item.content:encoded:
The Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden officially reopened its Hippo Cove exhibit on Monday, introducing new safety measures just days after the death of Fiona, the zoo’s famous 9-year-old Nile hippopotamus.

Fiona died on Thursday, Nov. 19, after swallowing a visitor’s knitted hat that was accidentally deflected into her enclosure. Zoo officials shut down the habitat "to give keepers space" following the incident, according to a Monday news release.

While Hippo Cove already met "strict" industry guidelines, zoo leaders said additional safeguards were installed before welcoming guests back.

"Even though the habitat already met strict standards set by the [Association of Zoos and Aquariums], we made some modifications to guard against something like this ever happening again," Cincinnati Zoo Director Dave Jenike said in a statement.

BELOVED HIPPO FIONA DIES AT CINCINNATI ZOO AFTER SWALLOWING VISITOR'S HAT

"We added a layer of netting above the viewing windows and, out of an abundance of caution, removed all ceiling fans in the area."

As the exhibit reopens to the public, visitors will be able to once again see Fiona's 27-year-old mother Bibi, 23-year-old Tucker, and her 4-year-old brother Fritz.

Zoo leadership confirmed the hippos are "behaving normally" amid the loss.

"They have been getting extra care, attention, a few more pumpkins, and according to the Zoo’s director of animal care, are behaving normally," the news release noted.

Despite the upgraded barriers, zoo officials stress that they still rely on guests to secure their personal belongings, take extra care near all animal habitats, and notify staff immediately "if they see something that shouldn’t be in a habitat."

ZOO SHARES NECROPSY FINDINGS FOLLOWING FIONA THE HIPPO’S HEARTBREAKING DEATH

"The Cincinnati Zoo has been accredited since 1978 and was last accredited in 2025 after an exhaustive inspection, a standard practice for Zoos seeking or renewing accreditation," Association of Zoos and Aquariums (AZA) President Dan Ashe said in a statement.

"Nothing was of concern for the hippo habitat in the inspection report. It seems like it was a freak event that couldn’t have been foreseen. Our hearts go out to all the professionals at the Cincinnati Zoo. I know they are [devastated] by this."

Macy’s also announced via its Instagram story that it will honor Fiona during the upcoming 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, according to People magazine.

"Fiona brought joy to millions, including so many in the Macy’s community in Cincinnati. This year, as Macy’s welcomes our own beloved Blue Hippo back to the Parade, we wanted to mark Fiona’s memory," the retailer said.

"With the Cincinnati Zoo’s blessing, Macy’s has made a donation to the zoo in Fiona’s memory and Blue Hippo’s handlers will wear a purple Fiona patch during the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade."

EXCLUSIVE: NIH FUNDED FOREIGN LABS WITH TROUBLING SAFETY LAPSES, INCLUDING DEADLY BAT VIRUS EXPERIMENT

Fiona captured the hearts of people all over the country after surviving an early birth in January 2017. Born six weeks early at just 29 pounds, Fiona rapidly drew enthusiastic online followers.

Her death occurred roughly a decade after another high-profile demise at the same zoo, when Harambe, a 17-year-old western lowland gorilla, was fatally shot by zoo staff in May 2016 after a young boy climbed into his enclosure.

Fox News Digital's Andrea Margolis contributed to this report.

item.title: You now have the option to watch the Super Bowl and halftime show in IMAX this Valentine's day
item.description: In February, Super Bowl LXI airs live in IMAX theaters for the first time, but questions over phones, live betting, and theater food could decide sales.
item.content:encoded:
This February, Super Bowl LXI will air live in IMAX theaters for the first time.

ESPN announced on Monday:

"ESPN, The Walt Disney Company, the National Football League (NFL) and IMAX have reached a partnership to bring the Super Bowl to IMAX theaters for the first time ever — giving fans a new, larger-than-life way to experience America’s biggest sporting event and the first Super Bowl in ESPN’s 47-year history.

"On Sunday, Feb. 14, 2027, ESPN’s telecast of Super Bowl LXI will be presented across hundreds of IMAX locations in the United States and select international markets, including Australia, New Zealand and Brazil. A milestone in cinema, it will mark the largest live event in IMAX history. "

The theatrical presentation will run more than four hours, featuring ESPN’s main Super Bowl LXI broadcast, Jay-Z's halftime performance, and pregame and postgame coverage.

There are some questions.

First, do standard theater rules apply? Do fans have to stay quiet during the game? If so, that is a problem for the more rowdy, drinking football fans among us.

READ MORE FROM OUTKICK HERE

What about phones?

Can fans use their phones during the game? Live betting is fully ingrained in how people watch football now. Having to walk out to the lobby every time you want to place a bet could be a tough sell.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Speaking of drinking, the food and drink menu inside the theater could decide whether fans actually buy tickets to watch the Super Bowl in IMAX.

Finally, is this a trial balloon for putting the Super Bowl on pay-per-view? Industry analysts have floated that idea for years, and the results here will be worth watching.

The IMAX screening is just one of several ways ESPN is airing the game this year. Alongside the main telecast, the network has already announced four alternative broadcasts: ManningCast (ESPN2), Field Pass with The Pat McAfee Show (ESPNU), Playbook with Next Gen Stats (NFL Network), and the Star Wars Funday Football animated telecast (Disney+, ESPN App, Disney Channel, and Disney XD).

Normally, the IMAX presentation almost guarantees Joe Buck and Troy Aikman on the call. Given the recent drama, though, ESPN is better off just promoting that Buck will be live in IMAX this February.

item.title: Wave of Hollywood home invasions has security experts urging less social media use and more privacy
item.description: Recent wave of high-profile home invasions in Hollywood has security experts urging less social media use and more privacy.
item.content:encoded:
As the holidays approach, a string of break-ins targeting the homes of actors, singers and athletes — some involving armed and violent assailants — has heightened anxiety across Hollywood.

On Nov. 18, the Los Angeles Police Department responded to a reported break-in at singer/songwriter Madison Beer’s Hollywood Hills home. Beer is the fiancée of Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.

Officers determined that no burglary had occurred. A day earlier, however, two masked suspects reportedly broke into tennis star Sloane Stephens’ home in Sherman Oaks.

ACTRESS MONET MAZUR'S $1.5M HOLLYWOOD HILLS HOME TARGETED BY MASKED SUSPECTS IN BREAK-IN ATTEMPT

The suspects shattered a glass door, alerting dogs and waking up the people inside the home, who called 911. Reports differed on whether those present were house sitters or Stephens’ mother and stepfather. A firearm was mentioned during the emergency call.

Stephens was away at the time. Police linked the incident to a second break-in later that evening at a Mulholland Drive residence once owned by singer Katy Perry. Following a pursuit that ended in Gardena, the LAPD took three suspects into custody.

HOMEOWNERS IN LEAFY ENCLAVES HIT BY BURGLARS ZEROING IN ON HIGH-END HOMES FOR SMASH-AND-GRAB SCORES

Meanwhile, Page Six Hollywood reported in mid-November that two armed assailants broke into the Los Angeles home of an unnamed prominent entertainment industry figure while he sat aboard a plane on an airport tarmac, preparing to head east. According to the report, one of the assailants struck his wife with a firearm while the couple’s two young children fled to safety.

The incidents have renewed concerns about burglaries targeting luxury homes owned by high-profile figures, often late at night.

Security experts say thieves can use readily available information, particularly social media posts, to identify targets and determine when residents are away.

"I always tell my clients to do something they are apparently incapable of doing — ‘Limit real-time information on their social media’," Herman Weisberg, managing director of Sage Intelligence Group, a security consultant and a 20-year NYPD veteran, told Fox News Digital. "I understand the importance and significance, but they really need to use judgment on sharing information that can be used to ‘virtually case’ their homes."

Some stars are taking notice, becoming more reluctant to have the financial details of their creative deals reported in entertainment trade publications, where such disclosures have long been common.

Weisberg said burglaries have historically tended to rise slightly ahead of the holidays, though he believes the recent incidents appear to be opportunistic.

ALLEGED BURGLARY CREW THAT TARGETED PATRICK MAHOMES AND TRAVIS KELCE HOMES ARRESTED IN ARGENTINA: REPORT

"Hopefully law enforcement will solve and make arrests which will provide more intelligence," he added.

The recent incidents follow other burglaries involving prominent entertainment figures. In 2025, the homes of Nicole Kidman, Brad Pitt and rapper Macklemore were broken into.

In 2024, the homes of Kansas City Chiefs players Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes were burglarized around the time of the team’s game against the New Orleans Saints.

"Entourage" creator Doug Ellin’s Beverly Hills home was burglarized in 2023. At the time, Ellin wrote on social media, "I know more people who have been robbed in the last six weeks than in the previous 30 years."

In December 2021, a fatal home invasion shook Hollywood when philanthropist Jacqueline Avant was shot and killed at her Beverly Hills home. Avant, 81, was the wife of music executive Clarence Avant and the mother of Nicole Avant, who is married to Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos.

item.title: Venezuelan illegal immigrant arrested in Utah after soliciting assassination of Trump, DHS says
item.description: DHS says an FBI tip led to the arrest of a Venezuelan national in Provo, Utah, over stickers urging the assassination of President Donald Trump.
item.content:encoded:
An illegal immigrant was arrested in Utah last month after an investigation linked him to the distribution of images encouraging the assassination of President Donald Trump, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced Monday.

Hector Alejandro Mujica-Hernandez, a Venezuelan national living in the U. S. illegally, was taken into custody in Provo.

Authorities said the arrest followed a tip from the FBI regarding online assassination threats against Trump that were traced back to Mujica-Hernandez's activity.

SECRET SERVICE ARRESTS ARMED VENEZUELAN MIGRANT NEAR WHITE HOUSE OVER ALLEGED TRUMP ASSASSINATION THREAT

"This illegal alien not only broke our laws by illegally overstaying his visa, but threatened the life of the President of the United States," Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said in a statement. "The Department of Homeland Security will not tolerate death threats of any kind."

According to DHS, the investigation centered on stickers distributed during a meeting of a group called "People of Provo Against ICE" (POPAI). The stickers featured rhetoric supporting Trump's assassination, including the phrase: "Shoot Trump, be a hero, become unforgettable."

DHS noted that the letter "A" on the stickers was stylized as an upside-down anarchist symbol commonly associated with Antifa and anarchist groups.

EXCLUSIVE: DHS SECRETARY MULLIN SLAMS SANCTUARY POLITICIANS AS ATTACKS ON ICE OFFICERS SKYROCKET

Trump has been the subject of several assassination plots, while U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers have faced an uptick in attacks amid the administration's immigration enforcement agenda.

"The media and the far-left must stop vilifying ICE law enforcement officers and President Trump," said Mullin, casting blame on both for threats and attacks against ICE and Trump.

Officials said Mujica-Hernandez originally entered the United States legally in July 2016, but remained in the country unlawfully after overstaying his visa.

item.title: NATO warns Putin could strike before European army responds, points to US as military model
item.description: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte warned Russia's war machine runs at full speed and could threaten Europe long after the war in Ukraine ends.
item.content:encoded:
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte warned Monday that creating a separate European army could undermine the alliance’s ability to respond quickly to a Russian attack, as Moscow continues to ramp up its military capabilities during the ongoing war in Ukraine.

Speaking at the 72nd annual session of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin, Rutte cautioned that competing military command structures could hold up decisions in a crisis, warning that Russia’s "war machine" is running at full throttle and could also pose a threat to Europe long after the war ends.

"What I would counsel against is having all the nations with their own militaries working together in NATO and then on top of that having a big European structure, because then if Putin attacks, we will first need two or three weeks to agree who will do what, and then he will probably end up in Rotterdam before we have decided. So that has been my argument," Rutte said, according to Ukrainska Pravda.

NATO JETS SHOOT DOWN DRONE IN LITHUANIAN AIRSPACE AS RUSSIA GROWS 'INCREASINGLY RECKLESS,' RUTTE SAYS

Rutte pointed to the United States as a model for an integrated military, arguing that European countries would also need to move beyond separate national forces to establish a unified army.

"My point has always been that if you have a European military, you cannot also have national militaries. The United States has one military."

"There is not a specific army or navy for the state of New York or for the state of California. It is an integrated United States military. If Europe is able to pull that off, fine," Rutte said.

Rutte said it was Russia's expanding military production and cooperation with China, Iran and North Korea that pose a long-term threat to NATO, regardless of how the war in Ukraine ends.

"We face great dangers coming from Russia and the fact that Russia works so closely together with Iran, China, and North Korea, we know that Russia's war machine at the moment is running at full speed," Rutte also said at the assembly in Berlin.

FOREIGN LEADER ON PUTIN’S DOORSTEP SOUNDS ALARM OVER IRAN FUELING MOSCOW’S WAR MACHINE

"Its war economy keeps growing, and it won't stand still when the war against Ukraine hopefully will end one day. That whole machine is there and will continue."

Rutte also rejected the idea that only countries bordering Russia or Ukraine face a direct military threat, warning that Moscow's long-range missiles put capitals across Europe within striking distance.

"Let me say once again to everyone here who is not on the eastern flank: I have news for you. You are on the eastern flank too. These latest Russian missiles need only five minutes longer to reach Lisbon, Rome or The Hague, my hometown, than to reach Tallinn, Warsaw or Helsinki," Rutte said.

"So we are all on the eastern flank here. Let's put an end to this discussion about whether or not you are on the eastern flank. We are all on the eastern flank."

The NATO chief's remarks came amid plans to deploy an early-warning aircraft to Poland after Polish prosecutors said three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles landed on Polish territory Friday during strikes against Ukraine.

NATO WARNS RUSSIA: 'WE WILL BREAK' FORCES, DESTROY 'ANYTHING AND EVERYTHING' IF YOU ATTACK

Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pawel Zalewski said that NATO would deploy an Airborne Warning and Control System, or AWACS, aircraft to strengthen surveillance along the alliance's eastern flank, according to Reuters.

"This is a very good system that gives us even deeper... operational awareness which allows us to respond better to this kind of threat," Zalewski told reporters following a NATO meeting in Brussels.

The aircraft can monitor large areas of airspace and provide allied forces with a shared picture of potential aerial threats, improving NATO's ability to detect and respond to missile and aircraft activity.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also warned Monday night that intelligence indicated Moscow was preparing a new wave of strikes against Ukraine.

Beyond Russia's ongoing military threats, Rutte said that Europe's interconnected infrastructure, including energy networks and communications systems, is vulnerable.

RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT

"We are all targeted, that we are all affected when it comes to our pipelines, our cables, our energy grids, and our economies."

"They are all interconnected, and that means that we are all in this for the long term. And therefore, we must step up to the plate to ensure that we stay ahead of danger."

Rutte said defending NATO countries demands civilian preparedness, pointing to northern European nations that have begun teaching residents about their responsibilities in the event of war.

"This really takes the whole of society," he said.

"And that's in the end, I think, still Norway and Sweden, and Denmark and Finland, and maybe one or two others who are really ahead of the pack here, and having made clear to their citizens what they need to do in case war breaks out, at least not to get in the way of the military, but to be helpful and also how they make sure that the police and the ambulance services and fire, the fire fighting departments work together, supporting the military wherever possible."

Rutte's warnings come amid uncertainty over Ukraine's long-term security arrangements and whether Western allies will offer guarantees resembling NATO's Article 5 collective defense commitment as part of a future peace agreement.

U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner said Sunday that President Donald Trump was willing to consider Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine as part of a broader postwar security arrangement for Europe.

item.title: Florida State makes its move with Glenn Schumann, but nostalgia alone won’t pay for championship roster
item.description: Florida State hired Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann after AD Jeff Purinton gave assurances on spending for the transfer portal and roster.
item.content:encoded:
Florida State spent the past few weeks zeroing in on one candidate to replace Mike Norvell. On Monday afternoon, the Seminoles landed their guy, reaching an agreement with Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann.

Both sides agreed to terms, with an expected announcement over the next 24 hours once everything is official.

Does the FSU brand still carry the same amount of weight that it did just a decade ago? No, but that doesn’t mean the Seminoles couldn’t attract one of the top names within the coaching circles over the past two seasons.

The Seminoles agreed to a five-year deal with the Georgia defensive coordinator, who is expected to stay on with the Bulldogs through the remainder of the 2026 season. ESPN first reported this news.

That part will obviously be tested over the next few weeks, as he tries to juggle the two jobs.

Hiring a 36-year-old coordinator with no head coaching experience might raise eyebrows among those who haven’t followed Schumann’s career.

But when you’ve spent years helping run Georgia’s defense and collecting national championships as an assistant at multiple schools, eventually someone is going to hand you the keys.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S QUIET SATURDAY TURNS INTO A BIG TEN DISASTER WITH BRUTAL CFP CONSEQUENCES

Glenn Schumann was a viable candidate for the North Carolina opening two years ago, before the Tar Heels board of directors decided that the Bill Belichick experience would be the better option.

That debacle in Chapel Hill looks worse by the day. For Schumann, it meant staying on Georgia’s sideline and waiting for the next opportunity.

Now, the former graduate assistant under Nick Saban gets his shot at leading a program that still has one of the most recognizable names in college football.

How highly does Kirby Smart think of Schumann? Bringing him to Athens was a priority when Smart took over at Georgia in 2016.

Florida State is now following a path similar to Oregon’s when the Ducks hired Dan Lanning away from Georgia.

Similar fire. Similar pedigree. Now comes the challenge of proving he can run the whole operation.

It also helped that Florida State athletic director Jeff Purinton knew Schumann from their time together at Alabama under Saban.

If the Seminoles could put together a financial package that would get them back near the top of the spending chart around college football, the coaching would take care of itself under the Georgia defensive coordinator.

The problem is that Florida State has struggled over the past few years since going 13-1 and being locked out of the College Football Playoff due to an injury to quarterback Jordan Travis.

And, a lot of that comes down to how much money the Seminoles are prepared to spend in hopes of competing for ACC and CFP titles once again. The brand no longer sells itself alone, which is the obvious case around college football over the past five years.

Multiple sources told OutKick that this was a main point of emphasis for the Georgia defensive coordinator when deciding on whether to accept the job. After meeting with Florida State officials on Sunday, Schumann needed assurances that the Seminoles were ready to provide him with enough money to attack the transfer portal and load up his roster with enough talent to win immediately.

Those assurances were given by athletic director Jeff Purinton, and Glenn Schumann will be tasked with putting together a coaching staff that can also make sure that expensive talent is not wasted.

COLORADO BOUGHT INTO 'COACH PRIME'. NOW DEION SANDERS’ LOSING COSTS MORE THAN THE HYPE CAN COVER

A team has to be willing to spend money to accrue enough talent through the transfer portal to at least on paper compete for a title. But, there are always risks when it comes to forking up $35 to $45 million for a roster.

Look no further than LSU, Texas A&M, Michigan, Ohio State and the countless others who are not in contention for the College Football Playoff this season, but have a roster that's worth over $40 million.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL SELLS ANOTHER PIECE OF ITS SOUL WITH CFP OFFICIALLY EXPANDING TO 24 TEAMS

But, if the Seminoles are going to get back into the fight under Glenn Schumann, they're going to have to spend.

With the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams and the business of college athletics constantly shifting, Florida State needs to start winning again.

The discussions about ACC schools potentially leaving for richer conferences over the next five or six years aren’t going away.

If the Seminoles want to command more money — whether from another conference or through a future arrangement within the ACC — they need a football program that gives them leverage.

Television deals with networks like ESPN and Fox will be heavily discussed within conferences looking to extract additional funds for their future spending. So, if you're going to take part in those conversations, a school had better be in a spot of leverage when it comes to football.

That starts on the field.

Right now, at this moment, FSU does not have the upper hand.

But that doesn’t mean they can't reignite the flame.

There is an obvious risk in handing a job this demanding to someone who has never been a head coach. Florida State needs a turnaround, and the pressure to deliver will arrive long before Schumann coaches his first game.

But there aren’t many candidates who can list Saban and Smart as immediate references.

The Seminoles have made their bet. Now they need to back it with the money, support and patience required to give it a chance.

Florida State wants back into the national conversation. Schumann gets the headset — and the responsibility of making people care again.

item.title: MS NOW host threatens to eject ‘tech bro’ guest during Jensen Huang debate, warns 'The door's right there!'
item.description: Stephanie Ruhle demanded respect during a heated MS NOW panel as Jason Calacanis defended Nvidia’s reinstated CEO against Yale lecturer Gautam Mukunda.
item.content:encoded:
MS NOW host Stephanie Ruhle rebuked several guests on Monday's episode of "Money, Power, Politics" for questioning each other’s credibility and demanded they leave if they refused to follow her rules.

Nvidia’s board unanimously reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO after input from senior U.S. government officials indicated his return poses no national security risk following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

President Donald Trump praised Nvidia's decision on Truth Social, calling Huang a "great patriot and a national treasure" while urging the chipmaker to complete its internal export-control investigation. But the guests on Ruhle’s show were more divided.

American internet entrepreneur and angel investor Jason Calacanis defended the reinstated CEO, arguing that someone as wealthy and successful as Huang would never risk committing treason.

TRUMP ‘DIRECTLY AND INDIRECTLY’ INTERVENED TO GET NVIDIA’S CEO REINSTATED, POTUS SAYS

In response, Yale School of Management lecturer and Bloomberg Opinion columnist Gautam Mukunda argued that there were credible accusations that Huang may have engaged in a criminal conspiracy to violate export control laws. He also dismissed the idea that the world’s third-richest person would not engage in such conduct as "absurd."

Calacanis interjected, dismissing the argument as "how Yale elites think." Ruhle immediately cut in to scold him, saying she would not allow guests to label one another.

"Hold on," she told Calacanis. "What we're not going to do here is say that because he works at Yale, he's some sort of elite. What we are not going do is label anyone. Just like I'm not gonna label you a ‘tech bro.’"

"I'm going to say ‘Jason's an investor who's here, and you're welcome to be here and share your opinions.’ But you're not gonna sit at my table and say ‘you're a Yale elite so you think this,'" she scolded before warning, "If that's what you're going to do, then the door's right there!"

TRUMP DEFENDS JENSEN HUANG'S CREDIBILITY, NVIDIA'S FUTURE AFTER BOARD REINSTATED CEO, SAYS 'SEX SELLS'

MS NOW business analyst Ron Insana then went after Calacanis’ credibility, saying he was "so tired of this Silicon Valley BS." 

As the panel laughed, Ruhle scolded her guests again and urged them to show each other respect.

"Give your opinion based on the facts that you know," she told Insana.

Fox News Digital reached out to Nvidia and did not receive an immediate reply.
